newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra sees good potential for key drugs.
newsitem.headline: Astra sees good potential for key drugs.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra said on Wednesday that it still saw good growth potential for its big selling drugs, ulcer treatment Losec and asthma drug Pulmicort.
"We estimate there is considerable growth potential for several of Astra's established products," the company's managing director Hakan Mogren wrote in Astra's annual report.
"Losec, which was the world's most sold drug at the end of 1996, has still a lower market share in the U.S. and Japan than in Europe.
"Pulmicort Turbuhaler is Europe's most sold asthma drug and will soon be launched in the U.S. and Japan."
Mogren said this potential and the entry of new products onto the market gave Astra an optimistic outlook for the future.
"My opinion is that Astra is very well placed for continuing future growth," Mogren said.
In 1996 total sales of Losec in the world amounted to 24.63 billion crowns and sales of Pulmicort rsoe to 4.73 billion crowns. Astra's full year sales reached 38.99 billion crowns.
